# okfctl

> A command-line tool for authoring and maintaining Open Knowledge Format (OKF)
> bundles. Pure Go — no CGO, no Python, no model runtime. okfctl does not author
> the OKF specification; it is a conformant consumer that enforces the spec floor
> and keeps anything stricter behind an explicit opt-in overlay.

okfctl scaffolds a bundle, adds and moves nodes without breaking links, keeps the
reserved `index.md`/`log.md` files current, checks a corpus against the spec, and
reports on its health and link graph.

## Docs

- [Command reference](https://okfctl.dev/_generated/reference/commands/): Every command, its flags, and a runnable example — generated from and kept in sync with the binary.
- [Concepts](https://okfctl.dev/_generated/concepts/): Bundles, nodes, the link graph, and the reserved files.
- [Authoring a bundle](https://okfctl.dev/_generated/guides/authoring/): From an empty directory to a validated bundle.
- [Curation health](https://okfctl.dev/_generated/guides/curation-health/): Using `lint`, `analyze`, and `--strict` in CI.

## Specification

- [Open Knowledge Format spec (SPEC.md)](https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/knowledge-catalog/blob/main/okf/SPEC.md): The authoritative OKF specification, owned by Google (`GoogleCloudPlatform/knowledge-catalog`). Where the spec defines behavior, the spec wins.

## Source

- [GitHub repository](https://github.com/cwest/okfctl): Source, releases, and issues.
